meta.title: ANATOMICA reproductive system inventory — Milestone 14
meta.source_tables: data/sources/bodyparts3d-4.0/ (BP3D 4.0 / FMA concept ids and names as released)
meta.counting_convention: One record per lateralised instance (right/left testis, epididymis, seminal vesicle), keyed on its instance concept with the side-stripped class concept carried as class_concept_id; one record for the prostate, keyed on its both-table concept; one record each for the corpus cavernosum, the corpus spongiosum and the glans penis, keyed on their IS-A concepts (the glans carries its zone concept as class_concept_id); one record for the mons pubis, keyed on its PART-OF-only concept; one record for the perineum and one for its anal part, keyed on their PART-OF concepts. The genital system root is a grouping class, censused but not a record. The perineal muscle concepts are cross-references to the muscular module, censused but never records here. Sex line is censused per concept and per record: the female line of the release is exactly one concept (the mons pubis) against fourteen male concepts — every internal female organ is absent from the release entirely and exists in this module only as sourced clinical records with the absence recorded (the Milestone 9 pattern). The urethra is not in this universe: it is the urinary module's single unsexed record (Milestone 12), cross-referenced, never duplicated.

sweep_rejected_names: left superficial dorsal vein of penis
right superficial dorsal vein of penis

sweep_adjudications.dorsal artery of penis: cardiovascular module class concept, carried there as artery.right-dorsal-artery-of-penis and artery.left-dorsal-artery-of-penis
sweep_adjudications.fornix of forebrain: nervous module: a cerebral fornix, not a vaginal fornix — the vaginal fornix has no concept in the release
sweep_adjudications.superficial dorsal vein of penis: cardiovascular module class concept, carried there as the right and left superficial dorsal vein records
sweep_adjudications.urethra: urinary module record 'urethra' (FMA19667): the release's single unsexed urethra concept, held by Milestone 12; cross-referenced by this module's male pathway record, never duplicated

totalsegmentator_overlap.note: of the 104 TotalSegmentator v1 labels (Milestone 3 census), NONE names a reproductive structure — there is no prostate, seminal_vesicle, testis, ovary, uterus or any other reproductive label in the index; the overlap of this module with TS v1 is exactly zero, derived here from the label index by term match and re-derived by the checker

absences.note: probe-based gap analysis, per sex line: each substring probe was counted over all six BP3D 4.0 release tables (zero hits = the name does not occur in the release); each exact-name probe was tested for a concept of exactly that name in either parts list. Present controls are interleaved in each line to prove the instrument reads the tables. The asymmetry is the finding: the male line's probes find the gonad, its duct's first segment, two of three accessory glands and the erectile tissues present and the duct system absent; the female line's probes find nothing but the control — the entire internal female tract is absent from the release

records.name: prostate
records.note: the only member the release files under its own genital system in PART-OF, and a singleton under 'organ with cavitated organ parts' in IS-A; keyed on the both-table concept

records.name: corpus cavernosum of penis
records.note: IS-A leaf. The penis itself has no concept in the release (exact-name probe-verified); the organ exists in the data only as its erectile parts here and its vessels in the cardiovascular module

records.name: glans penis
group_path: zone of corpus spongiosum of penis
records.note: IS-A child of FMA20247 'zone of corpus spongiosum of penis', carried as class_concept_id; the zone and the glans resolve to the same single mesh file (FJ3134, IS-A table — neither concept is carried in PART-OF), so the class carries no geometry beyond this record's

records.name: mons pubis
records.note: the only female-named concept in either parts list; the release files it in PART-OF under the pelvis, not under any genital root — there is no female genital tree in the release to file it under

records.name: perineum
records.note: PART-OF organ record: the release roots the perineum under the trunk. It carries the same four PART-OF mesh files as its anal part — exactly the perineal-muscle file set the muscular module carries for the external anal sphincter — so the release draws the perineum as its sphincter and nothing else (identity gated by the checker)

records.name: anal part of perineum
records.note: PART-OF child of the perineum; the release gives it the same mesh files as its parent
